context: Two sisters reminisce about their childhood home
purpose: Teach: 幾つ/およそ/まことに/どうにも/どれほど/暮らす/但し/かよう

lines.speaker: yumiko_mom
lines.jp: あの家で暮らしていた頃の写真、押し入れから幾つか取り出してみたの。
lines.en: I pulled out a few photos from the closet from when we lived in that house.
lines.style: Warm nostalgic tone, soft and reflective like a gentle older sister.

lines.speaker: naoko_aunt
lines.jp: 懐かしいわねえ。お父さんが厚生省の秘書官をしていた頃でしょう?どれほど忙しそうにしていたか、今でも覚えてるわ。
lines.en: How nostalgic. That was when Dad worked as a secretary at the Health Ministry, right? I still remember how busy he looked.
lines.style: Lively and warm, slightly teasing, the chattier younger sister voice.

lines.speaker: yumiko_mom
lines.jp: ええ。但し、家に帰ればただのお父さんで、庭でおよそ三十分は私たちと遊んでくれたわよね。
lines.en: Yes. But once he came home he was just an ordinary dad, and he'd play with us in the garden for about thirty minutes.
lines.style: Soft sentimental delivery with a small fond laugh midway through.

lines.speaker: naoko_aunt
lines.jp: そうそう。お母さんが食糧不足の話ばかりしてたのも、原油の値上がりが家計にどう及ぼすか、ずっと気にしてたからよね。
lines.en: Right. Mom kept talking about food shortages because she was always worrying how the rising oil prices would hit the household budget.
lines.style: Animated and analytical, mixing memory with grown-up understanding.

lines.speaker: yumiko_mom
lines.jp: まことに苦労していたと思う。物価指数のチャートを新聞から切り抜いて、雑誌のバックナンバーまで取っておいたのを覚えてる?
lines.en: She truly struggled. Remember how she'd cut price-index charts from the newspaper and even kept back issues of magazines?
lines.style: Quietly impressed, voice softening with admiration for their mother.

lines.speaker: naoko_aunt
lines.jp: 覚えてる。かような細やかさが、お母さんの家計簿にもちゃんと表れてたわ。マクロな話まで自分なりに勉強してて、本当にすごい人だった。
lines.en: I do. That kind of attention to detail showed in Mom's household ledger too. She even studied the big-picture stuff in her own way — she was really something.
lines.style: Reverent and reminiscent, slower pace as she searches for the right words.

lines.speaker: yumiko_mom
lines.jp: ねえ、お母さんが癌の検診に行き始めたのって、ちょうど新しい雑誌が刊行された年だったかしら。どうにも記憶が曖昧で。
lines.en: Say, wasn't it the year that new magazine started publication when Mom began going for cancer screenings? My memory's just hazy.
lines.style: Gentle hesitation, voice trailing as she tries to pin down a delicate memory.

lines.speaker: naoko_aunt
lines.jp: 確か、町内の懇談会の後よ。お医者さんが消化の不調を示唆してくれて、合成保存料を控えるように適宜助言してくれた、あの時。叔父さんが入国手続きを済ませて帰国した直後の、野球のシーズン開幕の頃ね。
lines.en: I'm pretty sure it was after that neighborhood meeting. The doctor hinted at digestive trouble and gently advised her to cut back on synthetic preservatives. It was right after Uncle came back through immigration, around baseball season's opening.
lines.style: Confident recall, voice brightening as the pieces of memory click into place.

lines.speaker: yumiko_mom
lines.jp: そうだったわね。究極的には、テレビも新聞もうるさかった時代に、静かに暮らす術を教えてくれたのは、やっぱりあの家とお母さんだった。あらゆる媒体に答えがないことを、相対的にちゃんと見て、何を保持すべきか分かってたのね。
lines.en: That's right. In the end, in an era when both TV and newspapers were noisy, it was that house and Mom who taught us how to live quietly. She saw clearly, in a relative sense, that no medium had the answers, and she knew what was worth holding on to.
lines.style: Closing line, tender and conclusive, almost like a whispered thank-you.
